Limitation: I don’t have the full PDF to inspect; I’m relying only on the two text chunks you pasted.

Exact contract language you supplied (ready to quote in the memo)
- MSA, p.4 §3.2: “either party may terminate for convenience upon ninety days written notice.”
- MSA, p.11 §7.1: “termination for convenience does not relieve customer of fees accrued through the effective date.”

Plain-English reading (preserve actors & terms)
- If the Customer (you) elects to “terminate for convenience” by giving written notice, §3.2 requires 90 days’ notice; the termination’s effective date will be the date the termination becomes effective under that notice (in ordinary reading, 90 days after notice unless the contract defines “effective date” differently).
- Under §7.1, terminating for convenience does not relieve the Customer of “fees accrued through the effective date.” That means the Customer remains liable for all fees that have been incurred/earned up to the termination effective date. In practice that includes:
  - fees already incurred before you give notice (outstanding/unpaid invoices), and
  - fees that accrue during the 90‑day notice period up to the effective date (unless another clause says otherwise).

How to quote both pieces in your memo (suggested, exact quoting)
- “Per MSA §3.2 (p.4): ‘either party may terminate for convenience upon ninety days written notice.’”
- “Per MSA §7.1 (p.11): ‘termination for convenience does not relieve customer of fees accrued through the effective date.’”

Practical points to confirm in the PDF before finalizing the memo
- Whether the contract contains any specific definition of “effective date” or “accrued fees” (those definitions can change the interpretation).
- Any other termination-related provisions (e.g., minimum commitment/early‑termination fees, liquidated damages, refunds of prepayments, SOW-specific termination, invoicing/cutoff rules) that could alter how much you owe.
- Any cure, offset, or setoff rights the Customer may have.

If you want, paste the definitions section or any other termination/fees clauses and I’ll check them against §3.2 and §7.1.
